data.name: BULLET SOUL
data.detailed_description:
A brand-new recipe for the shooting genre which blends classic shooting game design with a generous dash of modern day bullet-hell and flashy pyrotechnics: this soul food dish has it all! Play for survival and learn how your enemies behave, then switch to a more aggressive play style, and see your score sky rocket: destroying enemies at close quarters to build your multiplier, and see their bullets rendered harmless. Scour the stages for secret bonuses to push your score to even greater heights.

Music and Art
Bringing even more heat are Resonator: the moniker of aural wizards Kenji 'Itoken' Ito (Romancing SaGa series) and Kohta Takahashi (Ridge Racer and Ace Combat series), setting fire to your speakers with their tunes. Last but not least, Akio Watanabe lends his skills to the scene, bringing forth some fresh character designs.

Story
Mecha-warl, an empire of evil, who would use their military might to conquer space itself.
This is the tale of the brave few who stood against their threat.

Zenichi, the lone space pirate out for revenge.
Yun, the galaxy patrol officer charged with wiping out Mecha-warl.
Sadahl, the monarch who would challenge Mecha-warl in a bid for glory.
And Loop, continuing the battle for Earth, long after its defeat.

And so begins the struggle upon which the fate of space itself rests...

Bullet Soul arrives on Steam at last!

Features:
  • 4 different modes, including both DLC from the Xbox 360 original
  • 3 different ships, and a hidden second loop, complete with true last boss on Normal Mode
  • Practice and perfect your score stage by stage in Bancho Mode
  • Race the clock and the world's best scores in Caravan Mode
  • A 4th ship and further refined gameplay in Version B
  • Leaderboards divided by mode & ship with friend filters
  • Includes tate/vertical screen mode with X/Y scaling and smoothing

reviews.review:
It may be counterintuitive to give this game a thumbs-up while opening with a recommendation to [i]not[/i] buy it, but bear with me for a moment (or skip to the end of this text).

[b]Bullet Soul[/b] presents itself nicely, that's for sure. The selectable ships look cool, while the pilots are a bit overdesigned; points for Sadahl, for being a badass king. Enemy ships sport solid designs, with many non-bosses also being quite big, on top of being fairly colorful. The music is quite good, too. It's all just a bit unoriginal and unmemorable. And quite flashy at times, not in a good way.

The [i]tate[/i] mode, while always welcome, feels implemented hastily, as by default the portion of the screen occupied by the vertical modes is quite small and you have to fiddle with the settings to play with a larger viewport. Adding to that, the ending sequence is played horizontally no matter what.

Between a wider shot paired with faster ship movement, a more focused shot at lower speed, and bombs, the Cave template is evident. The main gimmick lies in the way enemy bullets are canceled. Usually, in other shmups, this is achieved only under specific conditions, like using a bomb or destroying bigger enemies; here, all it takes is for an enemy to be destroyed to see all its bullets turn into innocuous puffs of smoke.

Being built around this mechanic, the game encourages aggressive action, shooting down enemies before they can saturate the screen with bullets; some prioritization is required at times - you may prefer to save the big ship that has at least predictable patterns for last, because smaller enemies shooting from various angles are a more pressing matter. To further reward this playstyle, attacks are more powerful and more points are awarded the closer you are to enemies. Bosses have several destructible segments, and destroying them as quickly as possible ensures that their attacks can be extinguished just as fast.

As far as I've seen, this gameplay choice is a bit controversial among shmup fans, especially among the more skilled ones who see it as making the game too easy, but I won't fault the developers for trying something different.

Where I can find fault is in how the game, while overall playing pleasantly and smoothly, also feels quite by the numbers, with few really interesting passages or set pieces; the only one that is really memorable is a giant mecha that is ready to attack, and can even be shot briefly before a mid-boss rudely takes its place.

The characters are very unbalanced, with Sadahl being quite a bit more powerful than the other two pilots despite being the slowest. Version B, a remixed mode that was originally DLC, adds a fourth pilot named Loop, who is destruction incarnate (the first boss is totalled in seconds by her).

There are no selectable difficulty levels, and there are infinite credits - well, I'm not against the latter. A bigger challenge is unlocking the second loop, which requires finishing all five levels without ever using a continue, but after seeing a video of the true final boss, I don't even think it's interesting enough to justify that...

There is also a single ending sequence, or two if you count Version B; the only difference, depending on which character you just played, is that they appear over the movie and say something (in Japanese, without subtitles) before the end credits roll.

This PC port is also barebones, running at 720p only with no visual options, save for a forgettable smoothing effect that I'd rather deactivate. When the ending movie finishes, the game briefly flashes back to windowed mode and back (I've noticed that even in gameplay videos, so it's not an issue limited to my system).

All things considered, [b]Bullet Soul[/b] could have been more creative, but it's a solid "fast food" game if you just want to play a shmup for fun, while still having something for expert players who want to dedicate their time to it; at this point, it goes on sale for very little. So why the opening caveat? Because just a few months later, the upgraded version of the game was also brought to Steam, at exactly the same price, and includes a remix of this game's main mode. Unless you are a collector of the genre and such a maniacal player that you want to spot all the differences in the enemy waves and bullet patterns, you may skip this.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows7/8.1/10
  • Processador: Core i3 of Sandy Bridge generation or better
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Intel HD Graphics Series (It needs 1GB memory allocation)
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 3 GB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: Sound Devices compatible Direct Sound
  • Notas adicionais: XBox 360 compatible game controller strongly recommended
